lessonsIntro: Lynmouth is a rocky river-mouth point break for experienced surfers, and no surf schools teach here. If you're learning, book a lesson on one of the sandy beaches further west.

text: Lynmouth isn't a place to learn. Visit Devon describes it as an experts-only spot: rocky, often rough, and needing real care getting in and out of the water. The main wave is a left that peels off the eastern side of the Lyn river mouth along a cobblestone shore, and there is a rip from the river that pushes against the waves. It is often crowded when it breaks.

It also needs a big swell to work, typically when the open west-facing beaches are too large, and it is at its best in winter. If you're a beginner staying on Exmoor, the sandy beaches at Woolacombe, Putsborough, Croyde and Saunton have surf schools, hire and lifeguards in season. Come back to Lynmouth once you're comfortable paddling and reading waves on your own.

cards.title: Experienced only
cards.text: A rocky point break; not suitable for lessons or beginners.

cards.title: Big winter swells
cards.text: Works only on large swells, most often in winter. Sources differ on tide, so check locally.

cards.title: Rocks and river rip

hireIntro: There is no surf hire in Lynmouth, so bring your own board or hire on the sandy beaches further west.

text: Bring your own board. Surf guides suggest the main point suits longer boards and mini-mals, while a shortboard comes into its own on bigger, cleaner days. Sea temperatures peak at roughly 15-18C in mid-August and fall to about 8-9C in early March, so in the main winter season you'll want a 5/4mm or thicker with boots, gloves and a hood.

cards.label: Board
cards.title: Your own board
cards.text: Longboards and mini-mals on the main point; shortboards when it's bigger.

cards.label: Wetsuit
cards.title: 5/4 plus boots
cards.text: A 5/4mm or 6/5/4mm with gloves, boots and a hood in winter; 3/2mm or 4/3mm in summer.

cards.label: Other craft
cards.title: Not for bodyboarding beginners
cards.text: The rocky shoreline and river rip make this a poor spot for casual bodyboarding.

shopsIntro: Lynmouth has no surf shop, so buy or repair kit before you arrive.
shopsText: There are no surf shops in Lynmouth or Lynton. The nearest dedicated surf shops we could confirm are in Woolacombe, such as The Bay Surf Shop and Shore 2 Surf, and in Braunton, where Tiki Surf Shop sells boards and wetsuits. Plan to pick up wax, a leash or a spare wetsuit there before driving over to Exmoor.

lessons.q: Can I take surf lessons at Lynmouth?
lessons.a: No surf schools teach at Lynmouth, and local guides say it's for experienced surfers only.

lessons.q: Where's the nearest place to learn?
lessons.a: The sandy beaches at Woolacombe, Putsborough, Croyde and Saunton all have surf schools.
Only on big swells, most often in winter, when the exposed beaches to the west are too large.

hire.q: Can I hire a surfboard in Lynmouth?
hire.a: We couldn't find any surf hire. The nearest confirmed hire is in Woolacombe.

hire.q: Is there kayak or SUP hire nearby?
hire.a: OSKC Watersports in Combe Martin hires kayaks and paddleboards, but not surfboards.

shops.q: Is there a surf shop in Lynmouth?
shops.a: No. Woolacombe and Braunton have the nearest surf shops.
